prompt:
A crisp studio photograph, taken level with the base, of a colour-coded parts rack in a workshop: a flat base with THREE upright pegs standing on it, marked A (left), B (middle) and C (right).

It carries 5 round rings of clearly different widths -- ring 1 (the narrowest) is red, ring 2 is amber, ring 3 is green, ring 4 is blue, ring 5 is purple (the widest) -- each with its own size number printed large on its face. The stacking rule is the usual one -- a ring rests either on the base or on a ring wider than itself, never on a narrower one.

At the start the rings lie like this:
    - peg A holds, from the BOTTOM upward: disk 5, then disk 2
    - peg B holds, from the BOTTOM upward: disk 4, then disk 3
    - peg C holds, from the BOTTOM upward: disk 1

A child then played with the toy and a camera logged every move she tried, in this order:
     1. take the TOP ring off peg C and put it on peg B
     2. take the TOP ring off peg A and put it on peg C
     3. take the TOP ring off peg B and put it on peg A
     4. take the TOP ring off peg C and put it on peg B
     5. take the TOP ring off peg A and put it on peg C
     6. take the TOP ring off peg B and put it on peg A
     7. take the TOP ring off peg C and put it on peg B
     8. take the TOP ring off peg A and put it on peg C
     9. take the TOP ring off peg B and put it on peg C
    10. take the TOP ring off peg A and put it on peg B
    11. take the TOP ring off peg C and put it on peg B
    12. take the TOP ring off peg B and put it on peg A
    13. take the TOP ring off peg A and put it on peg C

The play does NOT get to the end of that list: at some point a logged move CANNOT be made, because it would put a wider ring onto a narrower one. Everything before that move is carried out; that move and everything after it is not.

Show the toy EXACTLY as it stands the moment the play stops. Every ring must sit on the peg it really occupies then, in the correct order; a peg holding no ring must be drawn empty.

Keep the picture clean: no move list, no annotations, no captions. The only characters in the image are the letters on the base and the number printed on each ring.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a workshop parts rack with stacking rings: a base with three upright pegs carrying round stacking rings of graduated widths? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_notext: The peg letters on the base and the size number printed on each ring do not count. Apart from those, is there a separate line of text or numbers that lists moves or states where the rings sit? Answer yes or no.
